data.title: Nigerian armed groups net nearly $6 mn in ransoms: study
data.description: ABUJA - Criminal groups in Nigeria raised nearly $6 million in ransom payments in the last year, a report said Wednesday, with two mass kidnappings by Boko Haram responsible for nearly 90 percent of the total.

data.title: How narwhal 'scientists' track Arctic warming
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The fight against climate change has a new, spiral-tusked ally: the narwhal.

data.title: Brazil sues Discord over child safety measures, demands $100 mln in damages
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - The Brazilian government on Wednesday filed a lawsuit to force the Discord messaging platform to adopt stronger measures to protect children, and is seeking almost $100 million in "collective moral damages."

data.title: Iran says US sanctions will achieve nothing
data.description: TEHRAN - Iran's president insisted on Wednesday that the United States would achieve nothing with its new sanctions campaign after Washington laid out plans to collapse the country's economy.

data.title: Dozens dead in catastrophic Nepal-Tibet floods
data.description: Hundreds missing as torrents of water and mud wash away buildings in border region

data.title: Prince Harry and family arrive back in Britain
data.description: LONDON - Prince Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children landed Wednesday in Britain, UK media reported, after the surprise news emerged last week they would be relocating from the United States.

data.title: Nile crocodiles in France hatch unaided amid heatwave
data.description: LYON - The heatwaves that have beset France have produced an unusual outcome at a wildlife park, where 10 Nile crocodiles hatched without human assistance for the first time, the director of the reserve said on Wednesday.

data.title: France eases cow diet rules to help cheesemakers
data.description: PARIS - Widespread drought and record-breaking heatwaves have forced France to relax some of its famously strict rules on cheese production, with authorities on Wednesday announcing special measures for abondance, beaufort and comte cheeses.

data.title: Nepal floods kill eight, cause ‘major casualties’ in Tibet
data.description: NUWAKOT, Nepal - Massive flooding killed eight people in Nepal on Wednesday as Chinese state media reported “major casualties” from a mudslide at a Tibet trade hub on China’s side of the nations’ shared border.

data.title: China’s coastal regions on high alert as Typhoon Saudel cancels flights, ferries
data.description: HONG KONG — Airports in China’s Zhejiang and Fujian provinces remained on high alert for potential delays and cancellations as Typhoon Saudel approached landfall on Wednesday, after multiple flights were cancelled in Taiwan and Hong Kong.

data.title: 'Our patron saint': Tennesseans mourn local hero, mega star Dolly Parton
data.description: SEVIERVILLE (UNITED STATES) - With Dolly Parton's "Jolene" filling the night air, fans of the late country music icon laid flowers at a Tennessee statue of the singer who changed their US state forever.

data.title: Iran says Hormuz strait still closed despite transit corridor talks
data.description: TEHRAN - Tehran warned on Wednesday that the vital Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened unless the United States ends fighting as it entered into discussions with Oman on a temporary transit corridor and mine-clearing.

data.title: Iceland to vote on resuming EU entry talks in close referendum
data.description: SELFOSS (ICELAND) - Icelanders are to vote Saturday on whether to resume entry talks with the European Union amid growing global insecurity, in a referendum seen as going down to the wire.

data.title: Drought-hit Danube gives way to fossil hunt in Bulgaria
data.description: RYAHOVO (BULGARIA) - Volunteers have been enlisted to scan the dried-up bank of the Danube in northern Bulgaria, close to where receding waters laid bare mammoth bones last month, with hopes of finding more fossilised fragments exposed by Europe's parching drought.

data.title: Australian police hunt thieves in massive oyster heist
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian police said Wednesday they were on the hunt for thieves who made off with hundreds of thousands of oysters.

data.title: At least 15 infants killed in Islamabad hospital fire
data.description: ISLAMABAD — At least 15 infants were killed when a fire ​broke ⁠out at a state-run hospital in Pakistan's ‌capital city Islamabad, triggered by a fault in air conditioning ⁠systems, local broadcaster Geo TV reported on Wednesday.

data.title: Coordinated attacks: Thailand's southern insurgency flares
data.description: BANGKOK - A surge in attacks across Thailand's south has once again placed a spotlight on the insurgency by Islamist separatists that has killed thousands of people over the last two decades.

data.title: High quality, low risk: record number of Japanese in Premier League
data.description: TOKYO - A record number of Japanese players are in England's Premier League this season, with clubs attracted by their proven quality, value for money and the "very little risk" involved in signing them.

data.title: Fave or flop? A guide to gauging video game success
data.description: COLOGNE (GERMANY) - The video game industry is notoriously tight-lipped about its numbers, filled with members-only metrics like wishlists, pre-orders and player numbers, so it can be hard to know which games have actually proven popular and turned a profit.

data.title: PGA chief says 'no current plans' for LIV stars to return
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive officer Brian Rolapp said on Tuesday.

data.title: Golf giant Callaway apologises after ad sparks outcry
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert, which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver.

data.title: Instagram chief admits touting teen safety tool while omitting it was barely used
data.description: OAKLAND (UNITED STATES) - Adam Mosseri, who oversees Instagram at Meta, admitted in a California court on Tuesday that he touted newly launched safety tools for teens without disclosing low adoption rates from early testing several years ago.

data.title: Social media use on the rise among Australian under-16s after ban: data
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian under-16s are increasing their use of social media apps such as Instagram and Tiktok despite a world-leading ban, data provided by a parental control software company showed on Wednesday.

data.title: Syrian Kurdish leader dissolves force that spearheaded jihadist fight
data.description: DAMASCUS - The leader of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, the Washington-backed group at the forefront of the battle against the Islamic State jihadist group, announced their dissolution on Tuesday under a deal with the government.

data.title: Canada hits back against Trump’s steep tariffs
data.description: OTTAWA - Canada on Tuesday announced counter-tariffs on US goods ranging between 15% and 50%, intensifying the trade war between the historically close allies.

data.title: Climate change becomes a scorching reality for Europe
data.description: PARIS - For generations, summer in Europe has been languid and dreamy, bringing fine weather and lengthy days on sunny beaches and terraces. But in 2026, the brutal reality of climate change forced its way into daily life.

data.title: Spain speeds up return of migrants from Ceuta
data.description: MADRID - Spain’s government took steps on Tuesday to speed up the return of thousands of migrants still in the Spanish territory of Ceuta following a mass influx from Morocco in July.

data.title: Iranians queue for petrol as US announces new sanctions
data.description: TEHRAN - Long queues formed at petrol stations in Tehran on Tuesday after the United States announced fresh sanctions aimed at pressuring Iran into submission.

data.title: Myanmar human rights conditions at new low, UN says
data.description: GENEVA - Human rights conditions in Myanmar have ‌sunk to a new low, with widespread abuses against the Rohingya minority and a booming illicit economy driven partly by illegal rare-earth mining deepening civilian suffering, the United Nations said on Tuesday.

data.title: Canada ready to respond to Trump’s steep tariffs
data.description: Canada is preparing to announce its answer to US President Donald Trump's latest wave of tariffs on Tuesday, as a trade war intensifies between the historically close allies

data.title: UN: One million Afghan children face ‘life-threatening’ malnutrition
data.description: GENEVA - One million children in Afghanistan are suffering from life-threatening malnutrition in a worsening new crisis hitting the country, the United Nations warned on Tuesday.

data.title: West Bank settlers attack AFP journalists
data.description: JANNATAH, Palestinian Territories - Israeli settlers in the West Bank on Tuesday attacked AFP journalists reporting on tension with Palestinians, in violence that left at least five people injured, the reporters and medics said.

data.title: World urged to rein in ‘killer robots’
data.description: GENEVA - The United Nations and the Red Cross warned Tuesday that the world is “dangerously close” to a future where so-called “killer robots” could target humans, and issued an urgent appeal for international regulation of autonomous weapons.

data.title: Europe's gaming bash kicks off as industry eyes 'Grand Theft' boost
data.description: COLOGNE (GERMANY) - Europe's biggest video games show Gamescom opens its doors Tuesday in Cologne with the industry hoping that the coming blockbuster "Grand Theft Auto VI" can provide a much-needed boost, as studios cut jobs amid fierce competition.
